articleBody:
Before ordering cabinets or scheduling installation, review this checklist to confirm your kitchen island plans are functional, safe, and code-compliant.

- [ ] Measure work aisle widths — Confirm at least 42 inches of clearance between island edges and opposing cabinets or counters to prevent kitchen bottlenecks.
- [ ] Map out appliance swings — Open refrigerator, oven, and dishwasher doors fully to verify they will not strike island hardware or block traffic.
- [ ] Determine seating overhang depth — Allocate 12 to 15 inches of clear knee space if you plan to incorporate barstools for dining.
- [ ] Plan concealed countertop support brackets — Ensure overhangs past standard limits have structural steel supports fastened directly into the cabinet framework.
- [ ] Identify dedicated electrical circuit paths — Plan underground or underfloor wiring for island receptacles, ensuring appropriate GFCI protection per local standards.
- [ ] Confirm plumbing supply and drain routes — Check how water supply lines and drain vents will route through your slab or subfloor if adding a sink or dishwasher.
- [ ] Verify floor levelness across the footprint — Level the underlying floor area so cabinet boxes do not twist, shift, or crack stone tops later.
- [ ] Select island task lighting fixtures — Coordinate overhead pendant junction boxes to align centered over the final countertop layout.

How to Use This Checklist:
Walk through your kitchen with a tape measure, blue painter's tape, and this list. Outline your proposed island footprint on the floor to test natural movement.
